positions.name: OwnershipVsRentedIntelligence
positions.frame: What distinguishes owned intelligence and the perspective one keeps from substrate that is merely rented or commoditized?
positions.why: Both expressions read in the same direction: a plain-spoken, technical maxim (register) that draws an antithesis (src-2's owned/rented contrast) and a metaphor (src-3's perspective-as-kept-asset) around one axis — what is possessed versus what is merely leased or commoditized. The relational read is market-pricing in both (proportionality between what's kept and what's disposable), the value read is autonomy/self-enhancement in both, and the affect is calm-positive/settled in both. There is a genuine conviction gradient worth holding in tension rather than resolving: src-2 registers as an argued claim ('is not the same as') while src-3 registers as bedrock principle ('the asset you keep') — the set carries both an assertion still being defended and a constitutive value being stated as identity-level, and the frame reads both as facets of the same ownership-versus-rental distinction.
